description: Hi! I'm a Computer Science sophomore interested in AI, programming, data analysis, and space exploration. I hope to collaborate with passionate people to build innovative solutions for real-world challenges. Our team plans to develop a Lunar Landing Site Navigator using NASA open data. We're looking for teammates with skills in Python, AI/ML, web development, 3D visualization, data science, or UI/UX design. Creativity, teamwork, and enthusiasm are always welcome!
summary:
LUNA-LINK is an interactive lunar mission planning platform designed to support the evaluation of potential landing sites near the Moon’s South Pole. By integrating NASA/JPL Moon Trek imagery and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Wide Angle Camera (LRO WAC) data, LUNA-LINK transforms lunar surface imagery into an interactive 3D environment where users can explore the Moon, navigate across its surface, and compare candidate landing locations.
The platform features real-time 3D globe interaction, selectable landing-site markers, coordinate inspection, configurable visualization layers, and a data gateway for NASA lunar resources. It also provides a GeoTIFF ingestion interface for future integration of Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation products.
LUNA-LINK addresses the challenge of making complex lunar exploration data more accessible and useful for mission planning. By bringing scientific visualization and mission-oriented data management into one interface, the project aims to help researchers, engineers, educators, and future explorers better understand the environmental and geographical conditions of potential lunar landing regions.
Our long-term vision is to develop a comprehensive lunar mission planning environment that supports terrain analysis, illumination assessment, Earth visibility calculations, and landing-site optimization.
details:
LUNA-LINK is a web-based lunar exploration and mission planning prototype developed to improve the accessibility and visualization of lunar scientific data, particularly for potential landing sites near the lunar South Pole.

The system consists of three major components:

1. Interactive 3D Lunar Visualization

The frontend is developed using Three.js and WebGL to provide an interactive 3D lunar globe. Users can rotate, zoom, and navigate the lunar surface while exploring candidate landing locations.

The system integrates NASA/JPL Moon Trek's LRO Wide Angle Camera (WAC) global imagery through a Web Map Tile Service (WMTS) data gateway. The imagery tiles are retrieved through a Python-based backend and assembled into a texture applied to the 3D lunar sphere.

Users can also enable or disable visualization layers, including lunar imagery, candidate landing-site markers, coordinate grids, and mesh wireframes.

2. Landing Site Exploration and Mission Interface

LUNA-LINK provides an interactive landing-site comparison interface featuring three illustrative candidate locations near the lunar South Pole.

Selecting a candidate automatically updates its geographic coordinates and corresponding information panel. The interface also provides mission date selection, regional navigation, visualization controls, and a dedicated area for future mission assessment capabilities.

The candidate locations are illustrative research interface examples and are not NASA-certified landing-site recommendations.

3. Lunar Scientific Data Integration

The backend is built with Python and FastAPI to manage external data requests and provide a unified interface for lunar data resources.

The current implementation includes:

  • NASA/JPL Moon Trek WMTS imagery retrieval.
  • LRO WAC global lunar imagery integration.
  • GeoTIFF file ingestion and optional geospatial metadata inspection through Rasterio.
  • A JPL Horizons connectivity and documentation interface.

The project is designed for future integration of LOLA Digital Elevation Models (DEM), enabling the conversion of elevation data into terrain-displaced 3D meshes. This would support more advanced terrain visualization and subsequent slope and terrain-obstruction analysis.

Technology Stack

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript.
  • 3D Visualization: Three.js, WebGL.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI.
  • Geospatial Data: GeoTIFF, WMTS, Rasterio.
  • Scientific Data Sources: NASA/JPL Moon Trek, LRO WAC, and the NASA Planetary Data System LOLA archive.
  • Astronomical Data Interface: JPL Horizons API documentation and connectivity endpoint.

Innovation and Intended Impact

Unlike conventional lunar image viewers, LUNA-LINK combines interactive 3D visualization, geographic exploration, scientific data ingestion, and mission-oriented interface design in a single platform.

The project emphasizes the relationship between lunar surface data and operational decision-making. Its modular architecture is intended to support future development of terrain-aware landing-site assessment, illumination modeling, communication visibility analysis, and multi-objective mission planning.

Ultimately, LUNA-LINK aims to bridge the gap between complex planetary science datasets and practical lunar exploration planning.
